payload.text: The Brennecke Institute originated the thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery concept, which uses the dopant to limit negative-electrolyte crossover and associated aging. Its confirmed gravimetric energy density is 148 Wh/kg, with a projected stack-level cost of $61/kWh at 500 MWh manufacturing scale. The chemistry cannot operate below 4 °C because the dopant precipitates from the negative electrolyte. Following an independent audit, the originally publicized cycle-life claim was retracted; the corrected governing cycle life is 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity threshold.
VERDICT: REJECT - the audit assigns the 80% capacity knee to 4,800 cycles, not 8,400 cycles.
